rules.sentence: Median nerve injury at the elbow or forearm can result in a single-palmar-crease appearance.

This finding reflects the combined inability to flex the index finger and distal phalanx of the thumb, weak flexion of the middle finger, and defective opposition of the thumb, all consistent with high median neuropathy.
Injury to the recurrent branch of the median nerve denervates the FPB, opponens pollicis, and APB.
Failure to recognize the motor deficit may result in progressive loss of thumb opposition and severe thenar muscle atrophy, which may constitute medical negligence.
